hypotheses: none — it is a method, not a theorem
attrs.note: FETCHED AND READ in R5.2, not summarized from the audit. The load-bearing sentence for this project is not the taxonomy: it is 'in eliminative induction, we never speak of evidence as directly supporting a claim; it supports a claim only to the extent that it eliminates doubts associated with the claim.' That is the strongest available statement of what R5, R5.1 and R5.2 have each rediscovered one layer deeper. Cited for the vocabulary and the structural rules ONLY; the Baconian m|n confidence arithmetic is NOT adopted, because combining eliminations needs a defeater-independence argument this project does not have.
attrs.result: Confidence in a claim comes from identifying and ELIMINATING reasons to doubt it, not from accumulating positive support. An eliminative argument has five elements — claims, evidence, inference rules, defeaters, argument terminators — and there are only three kinds of defeater, determined by the element attacked: rebutting (a claim), undermining (evidence), undercutting (an inference rule). The leaves of such an argument are terminated defeaters, open defeaters, or inference rules asserted to be tautologies.
